skill.name: browser-fingerprint-audit
skill.description: Audit browser and network fingerprint consistency with liarjs. Review canvas, graphics, audio, fonts, WebRTC, timezone, TLS, HTTP, and ASN signals.
skill.summary: Run and interpret liarjs browser fingerprint consistency audits.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: Three static findings are confirmed. Two commands execute a pinned npm package, while the default network path sends request metadata to liarjs.dev. Other detections are markdown or documented local behavior, but optional CDP attachment can access an existing browser session.

remediation.issue: The default scan sends network and fingerprint-linked request metadata to liarjs.dev.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before online scans, or make offline mode the default and describe every transmitted field.

remediation.issue: The instructions execute an npm package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before execution and use an integrity-verified package artifact or lockfile-backed installation.

remediation.issue: CDP attachment can control an existing browser and read its page state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, display the endpoint, restrict access to trusted endpoints, and warn about authenticated sessions.

content.value_statement: Contradictory browser and network signals can reveal automation or spoofing. This skill runs liarjs checks and explains the resulting consistency score.
actual_capabilities: Runs liarjs against a temporary local Chrome, Chromium, or Edge profile.
Evaluates 40 browser and cross-layer consistency checks.
Reviews canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, audio, fonts, WebRTC, and timezone signals.
Compares browser claims with IP, ASN, HTTP, TLS, and request headers.
Explains failed check identifiers, deductions, and overall classifications.
Supports offline checks, custom network endpoints, and explicit CDP attachment.
limitations: Requires Node 22 or newer and a local Chrome-family browser.
Online scans disclose request metadata to liarjs.dev unless offline mode or a custom endpoint is used.
The score measures internal consistency, not whether a specific website will challenge the browser.
Browser updates and unusual environments can change expected signals or produce baseline-specific failures.

use_cases.title: Review an automation profile
use_cases.description: Identify contradictory browser signals before using a controlled automation environment.

use_cases.title: Investigate fingerprint drift
use_cases.description: Examine canvas, graphics, font, timezone, and network mismatches after an environment change.

use_cases.title: Assess privacy exposure
use_cases.description: Run offline checks to understand which local browser characteristics are observable.

prompt_templates.title: Run a standard audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the default browser fingerprint audit. Report the score, classification, failed check identifiers, and concise explanations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first review of a temporary local browser profile.

prompt_templates.title: Run an offline audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the browser fingerprint audit in offline mode. Explain every failed local check and clearly list the skipped network checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when no browser metadata should leave the machine.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect selected signal groups
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this browser and focus on canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, fonts, WebRTC, and timezone. Explain contradictions and likely environmental causes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when graphics, locale, or network identity appears inconsistent.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing browser session
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my running Chrome through the CDP endpoint I provide. Confirm the endpoint and session access risk before attaching.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use only after explicit approval for an existing browser session.

output_examples.input: Run an offline audit and explain the coverage.
output_examples.output: The audit completed using local browser signals only. It evaluated 32 checks and skipped eight cross-layer network checks.

output_examples.input: Explain why a headless browser received a low score.
output_examples.output: The low score reflects observable headless and automation signals. It measures profile consistency and does not predict a specific website response.

best_practices: Use offline mode when external network comparison is unnecessary.
Prefer a temporary browser profile unless the existing session is the explicit audit subject.
Compare unusual environments with a saved baseline instead of relying only on an absolute score.
anti_patterns: Do not attach to an existing browser without explicit approval and endpoint confirmation.
Do not treat a high consistency score as proof that every website will trust the browser.
Do not send production browsing sessions or sensitive pages to untrusted endpoints.

faq.question: What does the score measure?
faq.answer: It measures consistency among browser signals and the network view. It does not predict every website's detection decision.

faq.question: Does the standard audit make a network request?
faq.answer: Yes. The online mode contacts liarjs.dev for IP, ASN, HTTP, TLS, header, and ClientHello observations.

faq.question: Can the audit run without sending data externally?
faq.answer: Yes. Offline mode runs 32 browser-only checks and skips eight network comparison checks.

faq.question: Does the default scan use my browser profile?
faq.answer: No. It launches a fresh temporary profile and removes that profile after the scan.

faq.question: Can it scan an already running browser?
faq.answer: Yes, through an approved CDP endpoint. That access can open tabs and read page state in the existing session.

faq.question: Why can a legitimate environment receive a low score?
faq.answer: Headless mode, datacenter networks, unusual fonts, locale settings, and browser version changes can create real consistency failures.
